questions.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ of three nails is drawn from a population. The population has nails of two different lengths, $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{10}\,\text{cm},$ distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the nails in the population have lengths $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{10}\,\text{cm},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $4+1=5$ nails only with the following lengths:

$$
5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm}\,10\,\text{cm}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot 5+10) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(20+10) \\  & =\frac{30}{5} \\  & =6\,\text{cm},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot {5}^{2}+{10}^{2})-{6}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(200)-36 \\  & =40-36 \\  & =4\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the sample size $n=3,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}=\frac{4}{3}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}≈1.15\,\text{cm}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.problem: If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{50}$ is a sample of size $n=50$ drawn from a population with mean $\mu =12$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=4,$ calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

Since the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=4$ and the sample size is $n=50,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}] & =\frac{4}{50} \\  & =0.08.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{0.08}≈0.28.
$$

questions.problem: If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with mean $\mu =24$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$  determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $0.5.$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Since the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{1}=1,$ we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.5.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} & <0.5 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{1}{0.5} \\ \sqrt{n} & >2 \\ n & >{2}^{2} \\ n & >4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=5.$

questions.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ of $n$ coins is drawn from a population. The population has coins of two different denominations, $$1$ and $$0.50,$ distributed in the ratio $1:4.$ Determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $$0.02.$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the coins in the population have denominations $$1$ and $$0.50,$ and these are distributed in the ratio $1:4.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $1+4=5$ coins only with the following denominations:

$$
$1,\,$0.5,\,$0.5,\,$0.5,\,$0.5.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(1+4\cdot 0.5) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(1+2) \\  & =\frac{3}{5} \\  & =$0.6,\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}({1}^{2}+4\cdot {0.5}^{2})-{0.6}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2)-0.36 \\  & =0.4-0.36 \\  & =0.04.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{0.04}=0.2,$ and we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{0.2}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $$0.02.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.2}{\sqrt{n}} & <0.02 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{0.2}{0.02} \\ \sqrt{n} & >10 \\ n & >{10}^{2} \\ n & >100.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=101.$

questions.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ of $n$ shirts is drawn from a population. The population has shirts of two different sizes, $8$ and $10,$ distributed in the ratio $1:3.$ Determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $0.5.$
questions.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the shirts in the population have sizes $8$ and $10,$ and these are distributed in the ratio $1:3.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $1+3=4$ shirts only with the following sizes:

$$
8,\,10,\,10,\,10.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(8+3\cdot 10) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(8+30) \\  & =\frac{38}{4} \\  & =9.5,\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({8}^{2}+3\cdot {10}^{2})-{9.5}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(364)-90.25 \\  & =91-90.25 \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{0.75},$ and we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.5.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}} & <0.5 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{\sqrt{0.75}}{0.5} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{{0.5}^{2}}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{0.25}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{3} \\ n & >3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=4.$
